newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART HIT FOUR PAST LEADERS DORTMUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART HIT FOUR PAST LEADERS DORTMUND.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart intensified the race for the German league championship when they came from behind to beat leaders Borussia Dortmund 4-1 on Saturday.

A 44th-minute penalty from Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov and goals from Dutchman Frank Verlaat, Brazilian striker Giovane Elber and Croat Zvonimir Soldo helped Stuttgart set up a tight situation at the top of the Bundesliga.
Just two points now separate the leading four -- Dortmund, Bayern Munich, Stuttgart and Bayer Leverkusen.

Reigning champions Dortmund, who went ahead in Stuttgart with an eighth minute goal from Germany defender Stefan Reuter, stayed on top of the table but Bayern drew level on points after a 3-0 victory over Schalke in Munich's Olympic stadium.
Stuttgart are now just two points behind in third, ahead of Bayer Leverkusen on goal difference. Leverkusen won 1-0 at home against promoted Arminia Bielefeld to stay firmly in the race.
